News.title: How to start a conversation on a dating app: The ultimate guide
News.content:
If you’ve found a dating app that feels right for you and have set up your dating profile, the next step is finding possible matches and starting a conversation (or two). Your first contact is a really important part of the process and will help you get off to a positive start on your dating journey.

But how do you open a conversation without sounding too keen, not keen enough, even cheesy or bland? Below, we share our top tips on starting a conversation on a dating app along with expert advice from sex and relationship coach, Angela Vossen.

What makes a good first message on a dating app?

If you have found someone you think you would be compatible with and want to get to know them better, take a close look at their dating profile before messaging them directly. Then keep things friendly and light while making any questions you ask open-ended ones. Sharing something about yourself will also make the recipient feel more comfortable sharing things with you too.

No less importantly, what should you avoid saying? Don’t focus solely on how your match looks in their profile photo. While attraction is important and compliments are nice, it’s far from the only factor that matters and focusing only on a person’s looks may come across as shallow.

How to start a conversation on a dating app

Once you have sent an initial message, try to maintain a good conversation. “Think of it less like performing and more like opening a door and leaving it ajar,” says Angela. “You’re not auditioning; you’re inviting. And the goal isn’t to dazzle; it’s to make replying feel easy and natural.”

She adds that good conversation has a rhythm of give and take, so ask questions out of genuine curiosity rather than firing them off like it’s a job interview. And share something of yourself too.

“Reciprocity is what turns an exchange into an actual connection,” she says. “And remember: timing and responsiveness matter just as much as what you say. Conversations fade not always because someone lost interest, but because someone lost attentiveness. If you’re taking 24 hours to reply, you’re essentially sending a carrier pigeon instead of a message. Show up. Presence is part of the seduction.”

Step 1: Analyse profiles for conversation starters

Look for shared interests and hobbies to discuss

Taking the time to read someone’s dating bio and profile information will help you lead with genuine questions and get the conversation off to a good start. Try not to get too personal too quickly, though. For instance, if their profile states that they are a widow or are divorced, don’t lead the conversation with questions about this. Sensitive subjects are better discussed in person when you have got to know one another better.

Identify key details to personalise your message

The dating profile of a potential match should have lots of key information, such as their hobbies, interests and photos. Use these nuggets of information to ask questions and start a genuine conversation. ‘I see you’re a keen runner and go to regular park runs. So do I,’ shows genuine interest while offering detail about yourself too. You could also ask them questions about photos they have shared on the app or something simple such as how their weekend was.

Step 2: Craft a unique opening line

Avoid generic greetings: Stand out with something specific

Starting a conversation with a very generic opening line such as ‘Hey, how are you?’ or just ‘Hello’ leaves the work of starting the conversation to the other person. Instead, lead with something more specific such as a warm introduction and an explanation as to why their profile stood out to you.

You can then ask a question that is specific to your match, such as, ‘I see from your profile that you’ve travelled a lot. Where did you go on your last trip? I recently got back from two weeks in France.’ In this example, you’re showing interest in them without asking anything too intrusive, and sharing more detail about your own life.

Using humour wisely to break the ice

Humour can be a great way of breaking the ice when used in the right way. For instance, you could say something playful such as, ‘I saw your profile and it looks like you’re a tennis player too. Maybe we should plan a game and see who has the better backhand?’ Alternatively, lead with something such as ‘I’m new to online dating. How are you finding it? Hopefully it’s about to get a lot better.’

Be mindful of being too sarcastic or dry initially as this may not always translate well over text or direct message. Humour such as this is best left until you have met in person and become more acquainted with each other’s tone and personality.

Discover more of the best pick-up lines

Step 3: Use open-ended questions to encourage dialogue

Open-ended questions encourage deeper conversation and allow the conversation to flow more naturally. Here are a few examples that will help you to get to know each other better:

Examples of effective open-ended questions

How would your friends describe you?

What are most people surprised to learn about you?

What’s the best place you’ve ever visited?

What are you most looking forward to over the next few years?

What are you most proud of?

What’s your idea of the perfect day?

Step 4: Introduce light-hearted and fun topics

Using ‘this or that?’ questions to spark interest

“This or that?” questions can be a really fun way of getting to know someone and are ideal for first dates or getting the conversation started. Take it in turns to answer questions such as ‘tea or coffee?’, ‘beach or mountains?’, ‘cats or dogs?’, ‘podcast or playlist?’ or ‘stay in or go out?’. The options are countless.

Fun discussion topics to make it reciprocal

Additionally, ‘this or that?’ questions will also bring up lots of different discussion topics too where you can expand further on your answers. For instance, if you chose mountains over a beach, you can explain more about why this is. Perhaps you went on an unforgettable hike that you would love to share more about. You could even use this game to decide where you go on your next date.

Questions such as ‘romantic dinner or active adventure?’ for instance, will make your dating experience fun and reciprocal.

Step 5: Be authentic and playful

Share a fun fact about yourself

Sharing a fun fact about yourself allows you to get more personal in a light-hearted way. This keeps the initial stages of conversation authentic without getting on to topics such as past relationships that may be too serious. This could be anything from a hidden talent to something unusual that happened to you such as meeting a film star or appearing on TV.

How to balance playfulness with genuine interest

Being playful and asking fun questions is a great way of getting to know someone new. Asking further follow-up questions about a light-hearted answer they have given shows genuine interest and a willingness to know more about them.

Step 6: Don’t hesitate to shift the conversation if necessary

Recognising when the flow dims

If you’re sensing that the person you’re messaging is losing interest on a certain topic, don’t be afraid to shift the conversation to something else. We all have hobbies and areas of interest that we’re passionate about, but it’s important to know when to change course. Have they started answering more briefly or less frequently? Ask them something about themselves to get the conversation flowing again.

Suggestions for smooth transitions to new topics

If you feel the need to move to a new topic of conversation, try and do this subtly and naturally. Saying something such as ‘On a completely different topic…’ before changing tack keeps things flowing without the chat grinding to a halt. If you feel you’ve overshared too early and sensed the other person feels uncomfortable, move on gently by saying, ‘on a lighter note…’ or ‘that’s enough about me. I’d love to know more about you.’

Step 7: Knowing when to move on

Understanding when interest is lacking

If you’ve been messaging frequently with a potential match and you feel that the interest is one-sided or they won’t commit to meeting in person, take note of this and don’t force it. There is no harm in making your intentions clear (such as that you would love to meet for a coffee etc) but if they don’t reciprocate or are vague in their response, place your focus on making other connections.

How to gracefully exit a conversation

If things aren’t going well (perhaps the conversation has started to slow or even made you feel uncomfortable), it’s absolutely fine to leave. The graceful way to do this is by thanking them for the chat and wishing them all the best in their dating journey. This makes it clear you’re moving on without being rude or leaving them feeling ghosted.

Likewise, if you want to keep the door ajar to a slow responder, write something such as ‘let me know if you ever fancy grabbing that coffee’ before leaving the conversation. This allows you to preserve your dignity without completely shutting down a potential connection.

Why is this important? Angela explains that not every faded thread is a rejection. “Sometimes it's just someone who got busy and felt too awkward to re-engage,” she says. Ending with a comment like this leaves the ball in their court and doesn’t sound rude or dismissive.

What to avoid with dating app openers

1. Unoriginal and low-effort greetings

No one likes to feel as if they are just another number in someone’s dating experience, so avoid sending generic and impersonal messages. You may think it’s a good idea to send ‘Hi, how are you?’ messages to lots of different people, but low-effort greetings such as this may not inspire the recipient to reply and engage further.

2. Being overly forward

Angela says that asking for a connection’s number before you’ve established any real chemistry or commenting solely on their appearance are two common ways of being overly forward on dating apps. Both can seem arrogant and shallow and may be off-putting to a potential match.

3. Not giving enough time for responses

Try not to send multiple messages before the recipient has had a chance to reply to one. Receiving a barrage of messages from someone they don’t know can come across as overly intense and place unnecessary pressure on a new connection.

4. Complaining or being negative

Complaining, being overly negative or so self-deprecating that it becomes a burden for a potential match to carry are all key things to avoid on dating apps. Try to keep the chat upbeat, positive and fun.

FAQs What is a good first message to someone on a dating app? Sex and relationship coach Angela says that a good first message on a dating app is one that proves you looked at their profile. “Not just at their photos, but at them – what they have written, what they have chosen to share, what that reveals about who they are,” she says. You can do this by referencing something specific and asking something open-ended. “Not, ‘what do you do for fun?’” but something that shows curiosity about this person, not a generic human. “It doesn’t need to be witty,” she adds. “It needs to be real. Pay attention to how their profile energy matches their messaging style. If someone’s profile is warm and playful but their replies are one word, take the hint and don’t over-invest.” How do I flirt with someone online? “Good flirting is playful, not performative – warmth plus a little wit, not a stand-up routine,” says Angela. She suggests doing this by complimenting specifically rather than generically. For instance, ‘You look so happy in that photo’ lands very differently to ‘You’re gorgeous’. “Referencing something they said earlier also signals that you’re actually listening, and attention is one of the most underrated forms of attraction,” she adds. “Forced funniness, though? People can smell it. Be yourself, even if your version of flirting is more dry or earnest than cheeky, that’s infinitely more magnetic than a persona that doesn’t fit.” However, Angela warns that you should spend so long chatting that you burn out the spark before you’ve even met. “If there’s chemistry, move towards actually meeting,” she says. “That’s where connection really happens.”

Sports.title: Wolves 0 Tottenham 1: Palhinha scores late winner to hand Spurs vital Premier League lifeline and first win of 2026
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM HOTSPUR secured a crucial 1-0 victory over already-relegated Wolves, delivering exactly when they needed to as Joao Palhinha struck late to seal a vital win.

It was a must-win game for Spurs following West Ham’s 2-1 victory over Everton, and Spurs could not afford to increase the gap between 18th and 17th place.





However the win came at a cost. Tottenham playmaker Xavi Simons added to the club’s injury nightmare after suffering a horrific knee blow during the clash and was forced to come off in the 63rd minute.

The Dutchman screamed in agony after going down in a tangle with Hugo Bueno before being stretchered off in visible distress.

Also, star striker Dominic Solanke came off in the 40th minute.

The Spurs striker was replaced by Richarlison after going down off the ball and receiving treatment from the physiotherapists.

READ MORE IN FOOTBALL 'IN THE WORDS OF RICE' Alex Scott's quotes Arsenal star in emotional Football Focus speech

However, the good news for Spurs came as Joao Palhinha came on to score the winner.

The goal was a close-range finish into the bottom right corner following a corner.

With Wolves and Burnley already relegated, it looks to be a head-to-head battle between Spurs and West Ham, as there are only two points in it.

Today’s 1-0 victory over Wolves is Tottenham Hotspur’s first Premier League win of 2026.



It has been an extremely difficult start to the year for the club, with this result ending a 118-day winless run in the league.

Their last top-flight victory prior to today was a 1-0 win against Crystal Palace back on December 28, 2025.

Sports.title: West Ham 2 Everton 1: Wilson scores dramatic 92nd-minute winner to snatch vital victory in Premier League survival race
Sports.content:
WEST HAM fans will learn one day that it is a silly idea to leave early.

The Hammers staged another late comeback to win through veteran striker Callum Wilson and rescue their Premier League survival hopes.





Things were looking pretty bleak until two minutes into added time at the end of the second half after Everton levelled and relegation rivals Tottenham scored up the road at Wolves.

From sitting pretty and inching closer to safety, suddenly the trapdoor was opening and West Ham were slipping back into the bottom three.

When Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall equalised for Everton on 88 minutes, thousands of daft supporters turned for the exits and headed for Stratford station.

It was just the same when West Ham went 2-0 down to Leeds in the FA Cup just a couple of weeks ago only for the team to pull it back from the brink and go to penalties.

Nuno Espirito’s side lost eventually but here they clung on to win and keep a two point gap on third from bottom Spurs with games running out fast.

Tomas Soucek had given the home side the lead 50 minutes into a drab match where nerves were clearly getting to them.

The Czech midfielder climbed between James Tarkowski and Iliman Ndiaye at a corner to score from a yard out.

He later produced another death-defying header to divert Ndiaye’s goalbound effort onto the crossbar in a huge let off.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

West Ham also rode their luck when Mateus Fernandes was let off for what looked like a clear penalty when he patted the ball while tussling with the Everton striker in his own box.

VAR Michael Salisbury can only have concluded the Hammers man could not see the ball at the time but it was a bizarre decision nonetheless.



Axel Disasi also hooked a shot off the line and West Ham’s luck ran out when Dewsbury-Hall barrelled home a shot from just inside the box on 88 minutes.

Spurs had taken the lead at Wolves six minutes earlier and an entire club’s medium term future was swinging wildly downward with time ticking away.

But deep into injury time left back El Hadji Diouf swung a cross to the far post where skipper Jarrod Bowen headed back across goal with Wilson unmarked to roll the ball home.

Sports.title: Liverpool 3 Crystal Palace 1: Reds up to fourth but forced to survive late scare after controversial goal from visitors
Sports.content:
ALEXANDER ISAK finally showed why he was worth all that money – and all that hassle last summer – as Liverpool surely booked a Champions League spot.

The £130million British record buy has spent most of the time since in the doldrums, including four months out with a broken leg after going on strike to get his move from Newcastle United.





With only two goals in 22 appearances, there were fears that he might never get back to being one of the most feared frontmen in the Premier League.

Yet just like that, he produced the stunning opener that lifted the cloud that had been hanging over him.

Not that his 35th-minute goal against a Crystal Palace side that had already beaten Arne Slot’s deposed Prem champs three times this season was the only highlight of this crucial win.

Nor was he the hero, although Andy Robertson contributed the second and £100m Florian Wirtz added a fine third with only seconds left.

For there is every chance Liverpool would not have climbed into fourth place in the table without the sensational display of third-choice goalkeeper Freddie Woodman.

With the game still in the balance, he made a series of stunning saves – and got himself injured in a brave dive at Ismaila Sarr’s feet – on the deck as Daniel Munoz clipped over him from the rebound in the 71st minute.

Slot was furious that referee Andy Madley allowed play to go on as Woodman lay in pain with a right knee injury.



But in the end that moment didn’t matter that much at all in what was an edgy victory.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

In the early stages, the loudest cheer around Anfield erupted at the end of a 60-second protest over planned ticket price rises by owners Fenway Sports Group over the next two seasons.

As part of a pre-arranged 13th-minute show of rebellion, home fans raised big yellow cards – 75,000 had been issued by various supporters groups amidst chants of “you greedy b*******”.

Hardly an atmosphere to inspire a nervy side that, even before that mass display of dissent, were given a bad fright.

Adam Wharton, surely the kind of midfielder Slot’s side have missed desperately all season, lifted a cross into the box.



Woodman, once a Palace ball boy and former academy player, didn’t react well in his first Prem start since arriving from Preston last summer as No3 goalkeeper.

With Alisson still not match-fit and his deputy Giorgi Mamardashvili out for the rest of the campaign with knee damage, there was no choice but to trust the 29-year-old although things didn’t start well for him.

But having left his line, he got nowhere near Wharton’s cross, Chris Richards rising in front of him but wasting a very decent opportunity.

After that protest, the fans fell almost dead-silent and their mood would soon grow darker for Mo Salah took a dive in a challenge just inside the box by Brennan Johnson.



The Palace man clearly got to the ball first before Salah hurdled him, took two strides, then dropped to earth.

Madley was advised by VAR Neil Davies to check the incident on screen but there should have been no real need – no penalty.

And suddenly Liverpool were ahead, suddenly Isak displayed the kind of talent that made him worth all that dosh.

The Swede barely had a touch as Alexis Mac Allister let fly with a wild, desperate shot that was going several yards off target.

But in the blink of an eye, Isak controlled with his right foot then swivelled to launch an unstoppable strike with his left.



Yet the back-slaps, in the end, had to be for Woodman.

He blocked Sarr after a defensive cock-up then dived brilliantly to his left to tip away Jean-Philippe Mateta’s superb header – bringing applause from Alisson, sitting amongst the subs.

Barely 30 seconds later Robertson had doubled the lead, streaking on to a long through ball from Curtis Jones before clipping past Dean Henderson and in off the inside of the post.

But Woodman, after that anxious start, was getting into the hero stuff, somehow clawing away Maxence La Croix’s header, crashing into an upright in the process.

Sports.title: Ex-Man City whiz, 26, who captained Foden to U17 World Cup glory reveals brutal reality of nine-year Premier League wait
Sports.content:
JOEL LATIBEAUDIERE captained Phil Foden and a host of England big-hitters to youth World Cup glory — then watched them become superstars.

Marc Guehi, Morgan Gibbs-White, Conor Gallagher and Foden are just some of the names strutting their stuff in the Premier League and Europe.





But the Young Lions skipper who held aloft that Under-17s trophy in 2017 in India was forced to take the long road.

Yet tomorrow the Coventry defender will lift the Championship trophy with his team-mates after their clash with Wrexham. It marks the end of a nine-year journey to join his mates in the promised land.

Latibeaudiere, 26, progressed through the Manchester City academy, spent a season on loan in Holland with FC Twente, followed by three years with Swansea and three more with Coventry.

He told SunSport: “Morgan was the first to text after our promotion was confirmed. I’m still very close with him. He’s always been in my corner and had a similar route, going through the Championship and getting promoted with Nottingham Forest.



“To see what he’s achieving now is great. He’s on fire, trying to get on that plane for the World Cup — it’s been good to see what the others have done as well.

“But to compare myself now to the likes of Foden, Guehi, Morgan, Conor, or those kind of boys, as a Premier League player wouldn’t do justice to what they’ve achieved.

“Maybe after a season, if I play enough games and get good minutes under my belt in the Premier League, I can say I’m in that category.”

The route to the top really began at that Under-17s World Cup, where Latibeaudiere learned leadership skills captaining a squad of enormous talent.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

ENGLAND’S CLASS OF 2017 — WHERE ARE THEY NOW? Where are England's Class of 2017 playing now at club level? CURTIS ANDERSON (GK): The hero of the penalty shootout against Japan. After spells in the US and non-league with Kendal Town, he retired from football in 2023. He’s now a financial advisor, helping the next generation manage their money. STEVEN SESSEGNON (RB): A versatile operator who left Fulham to find his own path. After various loan spells, he found a permanent home at Wigan in League One. JOEL LATIBEAUDIERE (CB): The skipper who finally reached the promised land. After nearly 200 Championship appearances, he is now a Premier League promotion hero with Coventry. Having captained England to glory, he switched allegiances and is now a mainstay for the Jamaica national team. MARC GUEHI (CB): A certified superstar. After captaining Crystal Palace to an historic FA Cup win in 2025, he completed a high-profile move to Manchester City in January. He is currently a regular for both the Premier League giants and the senior England squad. JONATHAN PANZO (LB): The former Chelsea starlet has become a true globetrotter. Monaco, Cercle Brugge, Dijon, Standard Liege and more recently Rio Ave are all on his CV. Never quite cut it at Nottingham Forest but now hoping to settle at Birmingham. GEORGE MCEACHRAN (CM): The technical heart of the 2017 midfield. He left Chelsea’s academy in 2023 to forge his own career in the EFL. He is currently playing for Grimsby in League Two. TASHAN OAKLEY-BOOTHE (CM): Another technical talent who took the long road. After a spell at Stoke, he moved to Blackpool in League One and Estrela da Amadora in Portugal. Currently with Dunfermline Athletic in the Scottish Championship. PHIL FODEN (RW): The undisputed jewel in the crown. A multi-Premier League and Champions League winner with Manchester City and England regular. MORGAN GIBBS-WHITE (CAM): Coventry captain Latibeaudiere’s close mate and a senior England international. He is currently the talisman at Nottingham Forest, where he recently fired them into the Europa League semi-finals and netted his first career hat-trick against Burnley. CALLUM HUDSON-ODOI (LW): After a successful rebuild at Nottingham Forest, his season was cruelly cut short by a thigh injury in April. Despite interest elsewhere, he remains a Forest player and recently signed a new deal keeping him at the club until 2028. RHIAN BREWSTER (ST): The 2017 Golden Boot winner has been plagued by injury. He left Sheffield United as a free agent in 2025 to join Derby. His first season at Pride Park ended early due to a knee injury in March after netting seven goals for the Rams. NOTABLE SUBS CONOR GALLAGHER: After a successful 18-month stint in Spain with Atletico Madrid, the ex-Chelsea kid returned to London in January, signing for Tottenham Hotspur in a deal worth £35m. EMILE SMITH ROWE: A fan favourite who left Arsenal in 2024 for a club-record move to Fulham. He remains their creative force in the Premier League, clocking over 30 appearances this season. ANGEL GOMES: The first player born in the 2000s to play in the Premier League. After five years in France with Lille and a move to Marseille, he returned to England in February for a loan spell at Wolves.

He said: “The talent was crazy but we got along so well off the pitch. Going to India for seven weeks, which was so foreign in terms of climate and food, was a great experience. It built a winning mentality at a young age.

“As captain, I made sure standards were met — turning up to breakfast on time, eating together, meetings on time. It can be tough for players not getting minutes when you’re on the other side of the world, so I tried to drive sessions and keep the boys hungry. You’ll see exactly that today at Coventry. I’m trying my best to drive the standards.”

The man now driving those standards from the touchline is Frank Lampard. He inherited a Coventry side sitting 17th in November 2024 and came within a whisker of taking them up last season before losing in the play-off semi-finals to Sunderland.

But this season — despite a mid-winter wobble — Coventry have ripped up the Championship.



Latibeaudiere said: “The gaffer commands the room. The biggest thing for him is his winning mentality. He wants to win everything, whether it’s a training game or a match. The team has bought into that.

“The intensity and quality he demands has taken my game up a notch. If a five-yard pass isn’t right in training, he’s on it. He knows how it feels in a game when you’re under the cosh because he’s lived it as a player and manager at the very highest level.

“A standout moment was when we suffered a few defeats and Middlesbrough overtook us. We had to play them at the CBS in February. The manager shared his experience playing for Chelsea in a huge game against Liverpool in 2003 on the final day that secured Champions League football and paved the way for their titles.

“Everything in the lead-up to that Boro game was top — and after winning 3-1 we never looked back.”

The promotion is a triumph for the whole club, including owner Doug King, whose ‘dad dance’ and fist pump celebrations after clinching promotion at Blackburn last Friday endeared him to the Sky Blue faithful.



Latibeaudiere said: “I had a chat with Doug after the game. He’s taken the club to a new level. Buying the stadium this season was massive because knowing it’s ours again has given it a different feel. Seeing him celebrating with the fans is what football is about.”

The human side of the club’s 25-year wait to return to the top flight was hammered home to the defender during a round of golf this week with team-mates Bobby Thomas and Carl Rushworth.

He said: “It was ladies’ day at a local club and a woman was waiting for us on the ninth green. She told us she’d been a fan for 25 years and what the club had been through since relegation from the Premier League.

“We sat there taking in what this means to the city. I’ve seen pictures from the day the club were relegated in 2001 of a guy with a sign saying ‘We’ll be back.’ I can only imagine how he’s feeling right now?”

Since that youth glory with England, he has also made the significant move to switch international allegiances, now proudly representing Jamaica.



But with the Reggae Boyz not at this summer’s World Cup, he has a summer holiday to Brazil planned with his girlfriend before taking on the challenge he has always craved.

He said: “I’ve never doubted myself. I always knew I’d play in the Premier League. We know how it will smack us in the face — but must see it as a massive challenge. Sometimes you get handed opportunities and you’ve got to take them.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

If a 2026 Latibeaudiere could speak to that 17-year-old boy holding that trophy for England, what would he say?

He said: “I’d have told myself, ‘You’re in for a hell of a ride!’ It’s not going to be straight uphill — there will be bumps — but you’re going to learn and enjoy it so much along the way!”

Sports.title: ‘Most disgusting & disrespectful thing’ says fans as Crystal Palace score in empty net after Liverpool keeper’s injury
Sports.content:
FAN FURY ‘Most disgusting & disrespectful thing’ says fans as Crystal Palace score in empty net after Liverpool keeper’s injury

FOOTIE fans were up in arms after Daniel Munoz got Crystal Palace back in their match with Liverpool.

The Colombia international got the Eagles back in the game with a 71st-minute chip over crocked Kop keeper Freddie Woodman to make it 2-1.





Woodman, the Merseysiders’ third-choice keeper, injured himself racing out to make a save before the ball fell to Munoz’s feet.

Referee Andrew Madley didn’t blow the whistle, much to the frustration of the Anfield faithful, which prompted Munoz to fire home.

Footie fans were fuming with Munoz’s decision to capitalise on Woodman’s injury and flocked to social media to express their dismay.

One wrote on X: “That’s the most disgusting and disrespectful thing you can do.

“Woodman is clearly down injured and they score on an open goal. Disgusting by Crystal Palace and Munoz.

“He celebrates too. If they don’t give Liverpool a goal now, I don’t know what to say. I don’t have words.”

Another said: “That Munoz goal is the worst fair play in history I’ve ever witnessed.”

And another said: “Munoz should have put the ball out.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

One remarked: “The definition of unsportsmanlike conduct.”

Another chimed in: “There’s no way the Munoz goal should be given.”

Some fans, however, defended Munoz’s actions, with one saying: “Nothing wrong with it.

“Not a head injury, so no need to stop play. Munoz has every right to go for it.”



Another said: “Munoz had every f***ing right to slot that, I’d be fuming if one of our players didn’t score that.”

And another said: “Munoz was right to put the ball in the net.

“It’s up to the referee to stop the game, and it’s up to our defenders to play the whistle.

Munoz wasn’t a popular figure among the Kop faithful after reducing the arrears.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Scores of Kopites shouted “Cheat, cheat, cheat” as he looked to take a throw-in in the 76th minute.



Munoz’s controversial goal mattered little as the Arne Slot‘s troops ran out 3-1 winners thanks to first-half goals from Alexander Isak, the outgoing Andy Robertson and a 96th-minute strike from Florian Wirtz.

Sports.title: Neil Warnock, 77, teases shock return to management as he shares picture from inside 41,000-seater stadium
Sports.content:
NEIL WARNOCK has teased he might have lined up a new job abroad after sharing a cryptic snap while hinting at a return to the dugout during a trip to Poland.

The 77-year-old posted a picture from inside an impressive stadium, sparking speculation he could be plotting a sensational comeback, this time overseas.





Fans were quick to play detective in the comments, with many claiming the ground is Legia Warsaw’s 41,000-seater home.

Warnock added fuel to the fire with a cheeky post alongside the image.

He wrote: “Just over in Poland with Kevin Blackwell where he’s working now. Seeing what it might be like to work abroad one day.

“Never expected anything as good as this, the stadium is amazing! Bonus points for naming the team.”

The veteran boss has been largely out of management but did answer an SOS call from Torquay United earlier this season but his stint lasted just 88 days.

Before that, his last major role came in 2024 with Scottish side Aberdeen.

Despite concerns about ring rust, Warnock proved he still had the magic touch during his short spell at Torquay.

He guided the club to two wins, a draw and just one defeat in his four matches in charge, steadying the ship during a difficult period.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Supporters flooded his post with excitement at the prospect of another comeback.

One wrote: “Warnock abroad? That would be unreal.”

Another added: “Go on Neil, one last job!”

A third joked: “Legia Warnock has a nice ring to it.”

Across a legendary career, Warnock has taken charge of a string of clubs including Sheffield United, Leeds United, Cardiff City and Queens Park Rangers.



And now, it seems the ever-colourful boss may not be done just yet, with a shock stint abroad potentially on the cards.

Sports.title: Xavi Simons screams in agony after stomach-churning knee injury as Tottenham fans say ‘this season cannot be real’
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM star Xavi Simons continued his team’s injury nightmare this season after screaming in agony with a horrific knee blow during their 1-0 win against Wolves.

The Dutchman was stretchered off after appearing to be in serious distress having gone down in a tangle with Hugo Bueno.





He was treated for a lengthy period by medics but was left in agony after trying out the knee once again and he was subbed for Lucas Bergvall.

It is the latest blow for Spurs amid their battle against relegation after Dominic Solanke went off injured before half time.

Tottenham fans couldn’t believe their luck after seeing their star playmaker getting stretchered off.

One wrote on X: “Well. Xavi Simons out for the season then. This season cannot be real.”

Another added: “Xavi Simons is in tears after a horrible looking knee injury. That looked nasty. Spurs’ injury woes just get worse and worse after Solanke already had to come off injured today.”

A third said: “Simons now down injured… what is our luck.”

One commented: “Who put this curse on Tottenham?! What is going on with this club.”



Others lamented the club’s “insane bad luck” as one added: “I’m done.”

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Spurs have already been without James Maddison and Dejan Kulusevski for the entire season, while Solanke, Bergvall, Rodrigo Bentancur and Yves Bissouma have been out for lengthy spells.

Currently, Tottenham also have Guiglielmo Vicario, Cristian Romero, Wilson Odobert, Ben Davies and Mohammed Kudus sidelined.

Thankfully for Spurs, they still managed to sneak a crucial 1-0 win at Molineux without Simons thanks to Joao Palhinha’s strike.



It was their first win under new boss Roberto De Zerbi and their first win full stop since late December.

Tottenham remain two points behind relegation rivals West Ham, who clinched a dramatic 2-1 win over Everton in stoppage time.

Spurs very nearly leapfrogged their rivals as Everton looked to have salvaged a 1-1 draw after Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall’s late equaliser.

But Callum Wilson netted in the final moments of the game to give West Ham in the advantage in the race.

Sports.title: Mo Salah may have played last game for Liverpool as he emotionally waves to Anfield crowd after suffering injury
Sports.content:
MO SALAH may have played his last game for Liverpool after suffering an injury.

And he emotionally said a potential final goodbye to the Anfield crowd.





Salah, 33, is leaving the Reds after nine trophy-laden years on Merseyside.

However, his farewell tour could be cut short.

The Egyptian picked up the apparent hamstring problem just before the hour mark in the Premier League clash at home to Crystal Palace.

During a stoppage in play, he fell down on to his back and then got himself back up.

Salah then walked off by himself, albeit very slowly.

And the forward notably and pointedly applauded all four sides of the stadium, taking in the love and standing ovation, before being replaced by Jeremie Frimpong.

After today, Liverpool finish their Premier League campaign with fixtures against Manchester United away, home to Chelsea, away at Aston Villa and, finally, versus Brentford at Anfield.



It means Salah has just four weeks until that Brentford clash, his final game as a Reds player.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And after more than 430 games and 250 goals for the club, Liverpool fans are desperate today’s injury is not his last showing.

One said: “Please tell me that’s not Mo Salah’s last Liverpool game. Praying nothing serious.”

Another wrote: “Mo Salah deserves a better sendoff than walking off injured. This is not how it’s supposed to end!”

A third added: “Let’s hope he gets the chance for a proper farewell.”



And a final user commented: “I hope this doesn’t turn out to be his last game for Liverpool.”

More to follow…

Sports.title: Tottenham relegation fears grow despite win as West Ham bag huge result in drop battle
Sports.content:
Tottenham relegation fears grow despite win as West Ham bag huge result in drop battle

The battle for survival at the bottom of the Premier League continued on Saturday afternoon with West Ham and Tottenham both fighting for points after Nottingham Forest's huge win

View 2 Images Tomas Soucek revels in the moment after scoring for West Ham against Everton (Image: Warren Little)

The games are running out for Tottenham. And the dramatic events of Saturday afternoon underlined why even an upturn in form might not be enough to save them as a late West Ham winner condemned them to another week in the relegation zone.

‌



Spurs did their part: they beat already relegated Wolves 1-0 courtesy of an 82nd minute goal from Joao Palhinha. Minutes after his goal, Everton even equalised against West Ham to propel Spurs to safety, for a few minutes at least.

‌



But Callum Wilson struck right at the death to clinch a 2-1 win for West Ham - leaving Tottenham two points adrift of safety with just four Premier League games remaining.

‌



Both teams suffered a blow before a ball had even been kicked with Nottingham Forest beating Sunderland 5-0 on Friday night. That statement victory put Vitor Pereira's men on 39 points, seven clear of Spurs and five of West Ham.

Mo Salah may have played last Liverpool game after coming off pitch injured READ MORE :

If Nottingham Forest's stunning result did light a fire under either team, then it failed to translate on the pitch initially. Both sides went in goalless, with Tottenham losing striker Dominic Solanke to injury in a first half where they failed to overly trouble Wolves.

Things got even worse for Spurs not long after play got back underway with West Ham taking the lead against Everton through Tomas Soucek.

‌



View 2 Images Tottenham beat Wolves but are still in the relegation zone (Image: Darren Staples/AFP)

The midfielder's header from a corner, given after penalty appeals were waved away moments earlier, piled even more pressure on Tottenham in their bid to bring points back from Molineux.

Xavi Simons was then stretchered off with what looked like a serious injury as Tottenham's afternoon took another devastating twist. But with time running out, Palhinha popped up to put Spurs on their way to what looked to be a priceless victory.

‌



Wilson, however, had other ideas: his intervention in added time wiped out Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's 88th minute goal to lift the roof from The London Stadium. A complete contrast to Molineux.

After weeks of damaging results, Tottenham can at least take solace from the fact that winning keeps them in touch of West Ham and, to a degree, Nottingham Forest, even it it was not enough to lift them out of the relegation zone.

Defeat would have been disastrous. Instead, Tottenham stay alive - for now.

Sports.title: Mo Salah injury worry overshadows Liverpool's win against Crystal Palace - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Mo Salah injury worry overshadows Liverpool's win against Crystal Palace - 5 talking points

LIVERPOOL 3-1 CRYSTAL PALACE: Goals from Alexander Isak, Andy Robertson and Florian Wirtz see the Reds move up to fourth, but Mo Salah may have played last game for the club

View 5 Images Mo Salah went off clutching his left hamstring (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Liverpool moved up to fourth in the Premier League with a third straight win, but their victory was overshadowed by an injury to Mohamed Salah. The Reds overcame bogey side Crystal Palace, who had beaten them three times this season, but lost Salah to an apparent hamstring injury.

‌



Alexander Isak put Liverpool ahead, bobbling a shot into the corner after the home side saw a penalty overturned by VAR for Brennan Johnson's tackle on Salah. Liverpool then offered a glimpse of their past, as Andy Robertson produced a perfect effort into the bottom corner to finish a sweeping counter-attack.

‌



The occasion took a turn when Salah was forced off with an apparent hamstring injury, in what could prove to be his final game for the club. Palace then pulled a goal back in bizarre and controversial fashion, with Daniel Munoz chipping into an unguarded net after Freddie Woodman was injured.

‌



Jorgen Strand Larsen nearly made it 2-2, but his effort hit the post and rolled along the line. There were a few more nervous moments, but Florian Wirtz sealed the points with a stunning injury-time strike as Liverpool saw out the game to leapfrog Aston Villa in the Premier League table and strengthen their grip on a place in next season's Champions League. Here are the talking points from Anfield.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool given clear VAR verdict after Mo Salah penalty overturned for diving READ MORE :

Liverpool fans protest against owners plans and make feelings clear with brutal chant READ MORE :

1. VAR gets one right

It does get forgotten in the modern age of online outrage and increasingly polarised viewpoints that, occasionally, VAR reminds you why it was first introduced. When referee Andy Madley pointed to the spot, Johnson must have felt relieved that VAR was in action and would save his skin.

‌



Salah's reaction suggested he wasn't convinced it was a penalty and replays showed that Johnson got a toe to the ball while sliding in to stop the Egyptian. Once Madley was sent to the pitchside monitor, it was a straightforward overturn - and a refreshing reminder of the power of the technology.

View 5 Images VAR overturned the penalty decision (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

2. Isak finally back scoring

Isak cost Liverpool £125million. His debut campaign in a red shirt has been nothing short of a disaster, with injury and a lack of fitness undermining his ambition to hit the ground running for his new side. But now finally ready, his time has come, with Hugo Ekitike sidelined with a serious injury.

‌



His first goal since December 20 - and his fourth in 21 appearances altogether this season - was not a pretty sight. His first touch from Alexis Mac Allister's shot cushioned the ball perfectly before his shot ricocheted fortuitously off the ground and over Dean Henderson's dive. It was his first in the league at Anfield for Liverpool - and fans will hope the first of many.

View 5 Images Alexander Isak scored his first goal of 2026 (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

3. Woodman steps up

No Alisson. No Giorgi Mamardashvili. No problem. When Woodman joined Liverpool from Preston in the summer, he would've hoped to get an opportunity, but he must have known it might never come.

‌



When it did, he stood up, while playing against the side he grew up supporting in south London. Liverpool's counter-attack for their second goal was started by Woodman's low save from a Jean-Philippe Mateta header and he made sure it was 2-0 at half-time by pushing away a back-post header from Maxence Lacroix.

The match started with a tetchy atmosphere at Anfield, with fans protesting an increase in ticket prices by holding up yellow cards, but there was a party atmosphere later on as chants of "England's number one!" went around.

View 5 Images Freddie Woodman had a good first half (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



4. Salah goes off injured

The celebratory atmosphere was impacted when Salah went down holding the back of his left leg following an inocuous challenge on the edge of the Palace box. The referee waved away a half-hearted appeal for a free-kick, before Salah signalled to the bench.

The medical staff rushed onto the pitch, and after a consultation, Salah walked off to a round of applause from the home fans, to be replaced by Jeremie Frimpong. With just four games left of the season, there are fears it could be his final appearance for the club, ahead of his departure this summer.

View 5 Images Arne Slot spoke to Mo Salah as he went off (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



5. Palace's controversial goal

The away side got back into the game in bizarre fashion when Munoz took advantage of Woodman being down to lob the static Liverpool defence and make it 2-1. Liverpool were furious with Palace for playing on while their goalkeeper was down after making a save one-on-one, but Arne Slot's defenders were culpable for not protecting their goal.

The officials only stop the game when it's a head injury and Woodman was able to carry on, meaning Slot didn't have to turn to his fourth-choice goalkeeper.

Sports.title: BREAKING: Xavi Simons stretchered off as Tottenham suffer another huge injury blow vs Wolves
Sports.content:
BREAKING: Xavi Simons stretchered off as Tottenham suffer another huge injury blow vs Wolves

Tottenham Hotspur have suffered yet ANOTHER major injury blow, as Xavi Simons left Molineux on a stretcher during Saturday's Premier League match against Wolves

View 2 Images Xavi Simons was stretchered off against Wolves (Image: X)

Xavi Simons suffered a horrific knee injury against Wolverhampton Wanderers on Saturday, as things go from bad to worse for Tottenham Hotspur. The Dutchman was included in Roberto De Zerbi's starting XI for the trip to Molineux, but lasted just 63 minutes after seemingly jarring his knee on the turf.

‌



Simons was racing with Hugo Bueno for the ball when his right leg got caught on the pitch, instantly falling to the ground in pain. After medical staff rushed over to treat him, the 23-year-old ultimately left the field on a stretcher, his season now likely over.

‌



Lucas Bergvall was called upon to replace Simons for the rest of the match, as a struggling Spurs chased all three points from their outing with a rock-bottom Wolves side. It comes as yet another major injury worry in an already depleted Lilywhites side.

‌



Sunderland VAR controversy explained as Nottingham Forest score FIVE in huge win READ MORE :

Guglielmo Vicario is yet to make his return since undergoing hernia surgery late last month, while Dejan Kulusevski is yet to make an appearance for his club this season as a result of a knee injury of his own.

Ben Davies is out for the rest of the season after breaking his ankle against West Ham in January, while Mohammed Kudus continues to recover from a thigh issue. Wilson Odobert, Pape Sarr and Destiny Udogie also missed the trip to the Midlands this weekend.

Elsewhere, Spurs suffered a major injury blow earlier this month when club captain Cristian Romero was forced of the pitch in a 1-0 loss to Sunderland AFC.

‌



The Argentine defender was attempting to shield the ball from Brian Brobbey to allow Antonin Kinsky to make a routine collection, when he was nudged in the back by the opposition striker.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

As a result, Romero's knee collided with the head of Kinsky, leaving both in need of on-field treatment. While Kinsky was able to play on after receiving bandaging to his head, Romero was less fortunate.

‌



The centre-half was immediately substituted off, with the extent of his injury coming to light shortly afterward; a partial ACL tear. As a result, Romero will not only miss the rest of the season with Spurs, but his contention at the World Cup this summer is also up in the air.

It comes as Spurs clinched a vital three points against Wolves on Saturday as they fight against the frosty grip of relegation. The Lilywhites had the opportunity to leapfrog West Ham into 17th with a win at Molineux, dependent on the mirroring result in East London.

While De Zerbi's men held up on their side of the deal, Joao Palhinha scoring the decisive goal in a 1-0 win 82 minutes into the outing, a simultaneous West Ham win over Everton saw the standings stay the same.

‌



View 2 Images Cristian Romero suffered an ACL injury against Sunderland (Image: Getty Images)

Tomas Soucek opened the scoring for the Hammers six minutes into the second-half of the match at the London Stadium, before Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall looked to rain on their parade with just two minutes of normal time left on the clock.

Callum Wilson's 92nd minute strike ensured that West Ham walked away with a much-needed three points on the day, much to the disappointment of Spurs fans worldwide.

‌



Due to the scorelines, Tottenham Hotspur remain 18th in the Premier League standings, two points adrift of safety with just four games to go.

Up next for the club is a tough trip to Villa Park come Sunday, May 3. Further clashes in May with Leeds United, Chelsea and Everton could then make or break Spurs' hopes of remaining in the Premier League for the new season.

Sports.title: Mo Salah may have played last Liverpool game after coming off pitch injured
Sports.content:
Mo Salah may have played last Liverpool game after coming off pitch injured

Mohamed Salah was forced off with what appeared to be an injury to his left hamstring during Liverpool's Premier League game against Crystal Palace

View 2 Images Mohamed Salah was forced off for Liverpool (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Mohamed Salah could have played his final game for Liverpool after being forced off with an injury against Crystal Palace. Salah appeared to injure his left hamstring in the second half of their Premier League game at Anfield on Saturday afternoon.

‌



The Egyptian star has announced that his season will be his last with Liverpool. He went down following a challenge on the edge of the Palace penalty area and immediately clutched his left leg.

‌



After being seen by the medical staff, he was replaced by Jeremie Frimpong in the 59th minute, with Liverpool leading 2-0 following goals by Alexander Isak and Andy Robertson.

‌



The 33-year-old received a warm round of applause from the Anfield crowd as he went off. He didn't appear to be emotional, which could suggest the substitution was a precaution.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool given clear VAR verdict after Mo Salah penalty overturned for diving READ MORE :

Liverpool fans protest against owners plans and make feelings clear with brutal chant READ MORE :

Liverpool have four games left in the 2025/26 season following the Palace game. Having been knocked out of the Champions League by Paris Saint-Germain, and the FA Cup by Manchester City, they are purely focused on the league and securing a place in next season's Champions League.

‌



Salah has 12 goals and nine assists in 39 appearances for Liverpool this season. He signed a lucrative two-year contract, worth around £350,000-a-week last year, but decided to leave early at the end of the campaign. He has made 440 appearances for Liverpool altogether, scoring 257 goals.

He announced his decision a month ago, saying: "I wanted to start by saying that I never imagined how deeply this club, this city, these people, would become part of my life. Liverpool, it's not a just a football club. It's a passion. It's a history. It's a spirit. I can't explain in words to anyone not part of this club.

View 2 Images Arne Slot spoke to Mo Salah as he went off (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



"We celebrated victory. We won the most important trophies. And we fought together through the hardest time in our life.

"I want to thank everyone who was part of this club throughout my time here, especially the team-mates, past and present. And to the fans: I don't have enough words. The support you showed me through the best time of my career and you stood by me in the toughest times. It's something I will never forget, and something I will take with me always.

"Leaving is never easy. You gave me the best time of my life. I always be one of you. This club will always be my home, to me and to my family. Thank you for everything. Because of all of you, I will never walk alone."

Sports.title: Liverpool given clear VAR verdict after Mo Salah penalty overturned for diving
Sports.content:
Liverpool given clear VAR verdict after Mo Salah penalty overturned for diving

Mohamed Salah thought he had won Liverpool a penalty in the first-half of the club's clash with Crystal Palace on Saturday afternoon, only for VAR to overturn it

View 2 Images Mohamed Salah saw a penalty overturned on Saturday (Image: PA)

Mike Dean has clarified that VAR was right to overturn Liverpool's penalty in the first-half of their match with Crystal Palace on Saturday. Mohamed Salah looked to have been fouled by Brennan Johnson in the Palace box just 23 minutes into the encounter, with referee Andy Madley instantly pointing to the spot.

‌



However, VAR swiftly intervened after scrutinising the footage, Neil Davies asking the official to approach the pitch-side monitor for a second look. While Madley was at the screen, Sky Sports Soccer Saturday pundits were quick to give their verdict for fans watching along at home.

‌



Tim Sherwood, explaining the process, said: "It's a breakaway from Mo Salah, he bursts forward, I don't think it should be given. Brennan Johnson is adamant there is no contact with Mo Salah, if he does it's outside the box.

‌



"I think he's dived, Johnson makes a dive and Salah goes over, he jumps straight over. Soon as he hits the floor, he's straight up Mo Salah."

Former referee Dean also added: "I don't think it's a penalty kick. I think Johnson's gone in to win the ball, Salah's knocked it past him, Johnson's got a touch on the ball, it's then hit Salah.

"I don't think Salah's even looking for a penalty, I just think he's lost his balance and gone down. So for me it shouldn't be a penalty kick - and if anything it's probably just outside as well."

‌



Madley ultimately back-tracked on his decision, awarding a drop ball for Dean Henderson to collect, while the Premier League Match Centre issued an explanation. They wrote on X: "After VAR review, the referee overturned the original decision of penalty to Liverpool.

View 2 Images VAR overturned the penalty decision (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

"Referee announcement: 'After review, Crystal Palace number 11 gets a touch on the ball. My final decision is a drop ball to the goalkeeper - no penalty.'"

‌



It comes as Liverpool eventually managed to secure a 1-0 lead at Anfield from open play, Alexander Isak finding the back of the net 35 minutes into the match. Andy Robertson also doubled down five minutes later, hitting it hard and low past Henderson from close range.

Isak has been tasked with leading the line for the Reds immediately after recovering from a leg fracture due to Hugo Ekitike's recent injury.

Ekitike ruptured his Achilles tendon during last week's match against PSG in the quarter-finals of the Champions League, and now faces up to nine months on the sidelines as a result.

Article continues below

As it stands, Isak is the first-team's only pure out and out centre-forward, although Arne Slot could also opt to utilise Cody Gakpo through the middle as he has done on occasion this season.

Sports.title: Liverpool fans protest against owners plans and make feelings clear with brutal chant
Sports.content:
Liverpool fans protest against owners plans and make feelings clear with brutal chant

Liverpool supporters continued their protest against their ownership over increased ticket prices during Saturday afternoon's home game against Crystal Palace

View 3 Images Liverpool fans protested against ticket price increases during the game against Crystal Palace (Image: Alex Livesey)

Liverpool fans have continued their protests against rising ticket prices, showing their owners the yellow card. Supporters at Anfield held aloft yellow paper, chanting, 'You greedy b*******, enough is enough' during their showdown with Crystal Palace.

‌



The Premier League champions have moved to raise general ticket admission annually for the next three seasons. The decision has angered supporters, who say the rise in prices are unprecedented and removes the scope for consultation.

‌



Liverpool say they are open to discussion with fans and are happy to speak to supporters about the matter with inflation being linked to the prices. It has been said that adult general admission season tickets will rise to no more than £1.42 per match, while operating costs at Anfield have risen 85 percent.

‌



Liverpool given clear VAR verdict after Mo Salah penalty overturned for diving READ MORE :

Rochdale vs York ends in dramatic scenes after pitch invasions and controversial goal READ MORE :

The supporter organisations including Spirit of Shankly, Spion Kop 1906, Kop Outs (LFC LGBTQ+ supporters group), cultuRED (faith and ethnicity supporters group), the LFC Women’s Supporters Club and multiple branches of the Official Liverpool Supporters Club co-ordinated the action, with the cards being distributed around Anfield ahead of the game.

The move saw yellow cards held up during the 13th minute of their Premier League showdown against Crystal Palace. Liverpool postponed protests during the Champions League second-leg against Paris Saint-Germain, as it fell close to the anniversary of the Hillsborough disaster, but protests on Saturday (April 25) increased after the initial protests against Fulham.

View 3 Images Fans held up cards in protest against the price increases (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA)

‌



A campaign van was stationed outside Liverpool's training ground on Friday and in locations around the city ahead of the showdown against Oliver Glasner's side.

A spokesperson for the campaign said: “This is about the future of Liverpool Football Club and who gets to be part of it. Locking in three years of price rises removes accountability and sets a dangerous precedent - not just here, but across the Premier League.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



“This isn’t ‘some fans’. This is hundreds of thousands of supporters making their voices heard. On Saturday, we’re asking everyone inside Anfield and beyond to show FSG the yellow card.”

Speaking ahead of Saturday's clash with Palace, who have beaten Liverpool three times this season, head coach Arne Slot said: "As long as I'm in football there are disagreements, and they are always about people with best interests of the club.

View 3 Images Liverpool supporters protest against the ticket price implemented by the club's hierarchy. (Image: PA)

‌



"Two weeks ago there was a protest and we had felt we had the full support of the fans. We will need the support of the fans."

After a slow start, the Reds turned on the style as they took a two-goal lead in the first-half. Alexander Isak scored on his first start in the Premier League at Anfield after returning from injury, before Andy Robertson netted, moments after Freddie Woodman made a superb reflex save at the other end.

Liverpool needed to continue their run of form after beating Everton last-time out. With another defeat for Chelsea in their previous outing at Brighton, Slot's side were looking to create a buffer to the Seagulls.

Article continues below

Fabian Hurzeler's side moved within five points of Liverpool but a win would see them leapfrog Aston Villa moving level on games played.

Sports.title: Rochdale vs York ends in dramatic scenes after pitch invasions and controversial goal
Sports.content:
Rochdale vs York ends in dramatic scenes after pitch invasions and controversial goal

York City scored a last gasp equaliser to beat title rivals Rochdale at the Crown Oil Arena and seal the National League title

View 3 Images Josh Stones scores the all important title winning goal for York City against Rochdale.

York City scored an incredible 103rd-minute equaliser to win the National League title in a dramatic ending to their all-or-nothing clash with Rochdale. The Minstermen had one hand on the trophy heading into stoppage time at the Crown Oil Arena with a draw enough to seal promotion.

‌



However, with the clock ticking down, the match descended into utter chaos. Mani Dieseruvwe scored a brilliant header in the 96th minute for Rochdale, sparking wild scenes and a pitch invasion. A win for Dale meant they'd go up as champions, and they thought they'd found an all-important goal.

‌



Veteran forward Ian Henderson came off the bench to produce a moment of magic. The 40-year-old curled the ball into the far post with the outside of his foot, and Dieseruvwe rose highest to power a header past York City shot stopper Harrison Male.

‌



I pulled off the National League great escape - but there is another big wrong to put right READ MORE :

National League stance on 3UP campaign clear ahead of Rochdale vs York City title decider READ MORE :

Rochdale supporters streamed onto the pitch to celebrate what they thought was going to be the title. After a five-minute stoppage, fans were cleared off the pitch and play resumed.

York then piled players forward and scored an incredible equaliser in the 103rd through Josh Stones, to seal the title in dramatic fashion.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Callum Howe's header was cleared off the line before the ball dropped to Stones at the far post. He bundled the ball towards the goal, and there were questions over whether it crossed the line, with York players adamant they'd found the winner.

The officials awarded the goal, and the travelling away supporters piled onto the pitch. There was utter pandemonium as York players, staff and fans celebrated wildly on the sidelines.

View 3 Images Stuart Maynard is mobbed after York City's 103rd minute equaliser sealed the National League title.

‌



Speaking to DAZN at full-time, York boss Stuart Maynard said: "They said it was 'York time'. Before Rochdale scored, it was 'Rochdale time.' There's a real belief and togetherness in this camp.

"You've just got to look at the fans behind us. When I first joined, I said we all had to be in this together; the players are warriors.

"When they scored, they're coming over to the dugout and said there's one more chance for us. There's a real belief from in us and it kept us going.

‌



"Everything went out the window. Everyone went up front, we had no one back. Kick it, then we get a throw and throw it forward. We know with this group they keep going to the end and they deserve it.

"See all these players behind me, they are incredible. They work so hard, tirelessly everyday. We're one big family and I love every single one of them."

View 3 Images Josh Stones is mobbed by York City fans after scoring the goal that won them the National League title.

Article continues below

As for Rochdale, they now need to pick themselves up and go again in the National League play-offs.

Jim McNulty's side will have a bye through to the semi-final stages and will face either Scunthorpe United v Southend United.

Sports.title: Palhinha gives Spurs first PL win of 2026 - but they stay in drop zone
Sports.content:
Joao Palhinha poked in a late winner for Tottenham as they picked up their first Premier League victory of 2026 in a 1-0 win at Wolves that gives them hope of survival.

It was a dramatic finale at Molineux even after the substitute put Spurs in front as Everton equalised against West Ham to briefly lift Roberto De Zerbi's team out of the relegation zone before Callum Wilson's late winner for the Hammers muted the celebrations somewhat.

But it just made the three points even more important for Tottenham on an afternoon when they lost Dominic Solanke and Xavi Simons to injury. They remain two points behind West Ham but retain hopes of staying in the Premier League - thanks to Palhinha.

Sports.title: Liverpool up to fourth but Salah injured in eventful Palace win
Sports.content:
Liverpool are up to fourth in the Premier League after earning a 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace, but Mohamed Salah may have played his final game for the club.

Alexander Isak scored his first goal since December and Andy Robertson doubled their first-half lead before Palace controversially pulled one back when Daniel Munoz lifted the ball over stricken goalkeeper Freddie Woodman, but Florian Wirtz struck in stoppage time to secure the points.

However, Salah, who announced he would be ending his nine-year stay at the club this summer, pulled up just before the hour mark after feeling his left hamstring, casting doubt over whether he will feature in the remaining four matches.

Image: Salah leaves the game with an injury

Arne Slot's side took full advantage of Aston Villa's defeat at Fulham on Saturday lunchtime, moving above them on goal difference and level with Manchester United, while building an eight-point lead over sixth-placed Brighton.

Sports.title: Birmingham see off Bristol City
Sports.content:
Bristol City interim Roy Hodgson suffered defeat in what is expected to be the final away game of his 50-year managerial career in the St Andrew's sunshine.

The former England boss watched his side lose 2-1 to first half goals from Phil Neumann and Jhon Solis as Tomi Horvat's late penalty turned out to be mere consolation.

The 78-year-old came up against a motivated Birmingham team looking to end their home campaign on a winning note and featuring three changes to the one which beat Preston in midweek, with Demarai Gray notably coming in for the injured Ibrahim Osman.

It took only eight minutes before the winger made an impact, taking a free-kick on the right and curling it into the box where he found Neumann unmarked.

Image: Phil Neumann of Birmingham City celebrates scoring his team's first goal

Ten yards out the German produced a cushioned volley that flew past Radek Vitek and into the net for this third of the season.

Eleven minutes later Gray thought he had scored himself when, with another more centrally-positioned set-piece, he went for the near post and struck the outside.

Then four minutes after that the Jamaica international was first to react to Carlos Vicente's cross at the back post but his connection lacked the pace to beat Vitek.

The Robins' goalkeeper could do nothing about Solis' 29th minute goal though. Blues boss Chris Davies had been urging the Columbian to press higher all game and when he did he immediately forced a loose touch out of Sam Morsy.

Solis volleyed goalwards and referee Robert Jones' watch told him the ball had crossed the line.

The visitors reshuffled at half-time with Rob Dickie coming on for Cam Pring but it did nothing to disrupt Birmingham's attacking thrust.

Five minutes after the restart Kai Wagner's corner was cleared only as far as Vicente 20 yards out, where the Spaniard slashed a bouncing ball goalwards that needed tipping over.

Two minutes after that Jay Stansfield threaded a pass in behind the Robins' defence that put August Priske in on Vitek and as the goalkeeper came out he lifted it goalwards - only to see his chip curl on to the upright and bounce to safety.

Seconds later Gray sent over a left wing cross that Priske met cleanly with his left foot but the shot flashed narrowly wide.

The visitors were given hope in the 82nd minute when Stansfield slid in on Horvat on the left of the penalty area and conceded a spot-kick. The Slovenian picked himself up and sent James Beadle the wrong way from 12 yards.

Sports.title: Segecic scores hat-trick in Pompey win
Sports.content:
Adrian Segecic scored a maiden EFL hat-trick as Portsmouth beat Stoke 3-1 in the SkyBet Championship to record a first ever victory at the bet 365 Stadium.

The Australian born Croatian gave Pompey a 32nd-minute lead and netted again after 66 minutes following Lamine Cisse's equaliser two minutes into the second half.

Top-scorer Segecic then completed his landmark treble with a 20-yard left-footed effort to wrap up the points eight minutes from time.

Portsmouth's last away win at Stoke came at City's former Victoria Ground home in February 1995.

Image: Adrian Segecic of Portsmouth celebrates scoring his team's second goal

And this rare success ensured Stoke, who were second earlier in the season, will suffer an eighth successive bottom-half finish since relegation from the Premier League in 2018.

Portsmouth, already freed of relegation fears, returned to action for the first time since their 5-1 defeat at Coventry which secured the second-tier title for Frank Lampard's side.

Austrian keeper Nicolas Schmid was one of five changes made by manager John Mousinho for Pompey's final away game of the season.

But within three minutes understudy Josef Bursik - starting for the first time since an FA Cup defeat by Arsenal last January - left the field through injury.

Ben Killip replaced him to make his first appearance since taking the gloves against Sheffield Wednesday last September.

Around 3,000 Pompey fans, celebrating their recent Championship survival, were enjoying themselves even if the action was less enthralling.

But 13 minutes from the break the visitors went ahead through former A-League talisman Segecic.

Collecting a threaded through pass from Harvey Blair, the ex Sydney FC star had time before rifling a rising left-footed shot beyond Tommy Simkin for his eighth goal of the season.

Stoke rallied before half-time with Cisse's back post effort via a Sorba Thomas cross denied by Killip.

As the ball bounced around the six-yard box Spurs loanee Ash Phillips and Cisse could not force it over the line.

But there was little surprise when the home side was booed off at the break.

Those jeers quickly turned to cheers three minutes after the restart as Cisse headed in an in-swinging corner from player-of-the-season Thomas.

Segecic went close to restoring Pompey's lead after 62 minutes but headed into the side netting.

He made no mistake though four minutes later. Josh Murphy crossed from the Stoke right, Colby Bishop could not get a touch but Segecic nipped ahead of Ben Gibson to stab the ball home from three yards.

Full-back Jordan Williams almost made it 3-1 but put his shot fractionally wide of Simkin's right hand upright.

However Segecic, 21, rounded off a memorable individual display with his third goal and fourth in two games.

Sports.title: Oxford relegated but see off Sheff Wed
Sports.content:
Will Lankshear scored twice as Oxford beat Sheffield Wednesday 4-1 in the battle of the already-relegated Championship clubs at the Kassam Stadium.

Oxford's relegation had been confirmed earlier in the afternoon when Charlton beat Hull, following on from West Brom's goalless draw against Ipswich, meaning that United's two-year stay in the second tier was over.

With one match of the season to go, Wednesday still have only one victory to their name, and they were comprehensively outplayed by Oxford.

Lankshear put Matt Bloomfield's team into a sixth-minute lead when he met Stan Mills' low cross from the right with a skilful flick past keeper Pierce Charles at the near post.

Image: Will Lankshear of Oxford United celebrates scoring his sides second goal

The Tottenham loanee then took his tally for the season to 12 - 11 of them in the Championship - with a curling 25-yard shot over Charles and into the top corner in the 27th minute.

Former Sheffield Wednesday midfielder Will Vaulks made it three with a thumping left-footed shot, after controlling the ball neatly with his right, in the 66th minute - his first goal of the campaign.

Substitute Will Grainger pulled one back for the Owls on 72 minutes with a smart 20-yard shot high into the net.

Yet Oxford restored their three-goal advantage a minute later when Myles Peart-Harris swivelled and shot past Charles from 14 yards.

A run of three straight wins in March had given the U's real hope of staying up but successive 1-0 defeats to Derby and Wrexham earlier this month in the end proved fatal.

The Owls had known their fate for months, yet their fans still filled out the 1,500-capacity away section, dozens of them dressed as bananas.

It was a fine low cross from Mills that set up the chance for Lankshear who produced a finish to match.

As the home side dominated, only a superb block by Nathaniel Chalobah prevented Michal Helik from making it 2-0.

Lankshear did soon double Oxford's lead, however, with his brilliant individual effort.

Jamal Lowe delivered Wednesday's first effort on target with a shot that Jamie Cumming got right behind.

Before the break, Charlie McNeill produced a smart turn to outfox two markers, and he was unlucky to see his shot hit the outside of the post.

Sports.title: Wilson's late strike sees West Ham edge Everton to stay out of drop zone
Sports.content:
Callum Wilson came off the bench to score in stoppage time as West Ham beat Everton 2-1 to stay out of the Premier League relegation zone.

On a topsy-turvy afternoon in the capital, Nuno Espirito Santo's side had appeared to be cruising to a huge three points thanks to Tomas Soucek's 51st-minute header, until late drama.

Firstly, as news of a Tottenham Hotspur goal at Wolves filtered around the London Stadium, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall volleyed the visitors level with just two minutes to go, pushing the Hammers into the drop zone on goal difference.

Team news headlines Nuno named the same XI that drew at Crystal Palace on MNF

Everton brought in Thierno Barry and Michael Keane for the concussed Beto and Jarrad Branthwaite, who is out for the remainder of the season with a hamstring injury

But just as the board was raised to indicate there would be another eight minutes of added time, up popped the ever-green Wilson to score after good work at the back post by Jarrod Bowen, a vital strike that saw West Ham again leapfrog their London rivals and to safety - for now.
